notes: Actual revenues and expenditures for fiscal year 2023-24 (ending June 30, 2024), as the county reported them to the State Controller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Counties provide social services, public health, jails and courts for everyone in the county, and city-type services in unincorporated areas.
Water, sewer, electric, gas and solid waste utilities count as utilities; airports, ports and transit as infrastructure; public hospitals as health services.
Counties report capital outlay by fund rather than by service, so it counts as infrastructure.

Internal service funds (charges between departments), depreciation and transfers between funds are left out. Enterprise funds' interest is replaced by their principal and interest payments from the debt forms.
Courts, legal services, prosecutors and public defenders, housing, planning and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, certificates of participation, other long-term debt, construction financing and leases, as reported.
Political money is not scored: California county candidates file campaign reports with their local filing officer, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for California yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: As of 2022, the Sonoma County Sheriff's Office did not have automated license plate readers, but accessed ALPR data through a regional auto theft task force.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000928, citing Sonoma County Sheriff's Office

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Sonoma County Sheriff's Office operated 13 drones as of 2023.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003860, citing Sonoma County Sheriff's Office

notes: Actual revenues and expenditures for fiscal year 2023-24 (ending June 30, 2024), as the city reported them to the State Controller. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Sonoma County.
Water, sewer, electric, gas and solid waste utilities count as utilities; airports, ports and transit as infrastructure; public hospitals as health services.

Internal service funds (charges between departments), depreciation and transfers between funds are left out. Enterprise funds' interest is replaced by their principal and interest payments from the debt forms.
Courts, legal services, prosecutors and public defenders, housing, planning and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, certificates of participation, other long-term debt, construction financing and leases, as reported.
Political money is not scored: California city candidates file campaign reports with their local filing officer, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 12 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Sonoma's borders in OpenStreetMap (10 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for California yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 10 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Sonoma's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
